ideas.risks: The naive condition rho_n=o(n) may be too weak: compactness may only control fixed horizons after subsequence extraction. Strict-crossing discontinuities also need a left-limit compactification or eta-implementation.
ideas.summary: Turn the solver's finite-prefix LP into an infinite-policy theorem. Define a normalized feasibility quantity such as inf over mu_1,...,mu_{n-1} of max_{T<=n, T>=N} R_T/T, then prove or refute equivalence between this tending to 0 and existence of one horizon-oblivious randomized policy with R_T=o(T) on the deterministic known path.
ideas.title: Compactness For The Prefix LP
ideas.why_promising: This would convert the solver's exact but tautological marginal condition into a precise finite-to-infinite characterization, and it directly targets the main gap in the current solver attempt.

ideas.risks: The dual may remain computational rather than structural. Strong duality needs finite support or left-limit action space, and V_T^* must be handled as a supremum under strict crossing.
ideas.summary: Derive the exact minimax dual of the finite-prefix problem: min_mu max_{T<=n} [V_T^* - sum_{t<T} g_{mu_t}(M_{t,T})] equals max over horizon weights lambda of sum_T lambda_T V_T^* minus sum_t sup_a sum_{T>t} lambda_T a 1{a<M_{t,T}}. Then interpret dual optimizers as decision-relevant horizon-conflict certificates.
ideas.title: Finite-Prefix Dual Certificates
ideas.why_promising: This generalizes the kappa dual from terminal blocks to arbitrary deterministic paths and may give the right replacement for loose suffix-menu sums.

ideas.risks: The comparator sup_a E[...] couples histories globally, so per-history LPs may not compose cleanly. The result may become a stochastic-control tautology unless the dual exposes a simple information modulus.
ideas.summary: Extend the exact marginal reduction from deterministic paths to exogenous stochastic processes. For policy kernels mu_t(.|history), condition on H_t and write rewards through conditional suffix-max laws P(M_{t,T}>a | H_t). Develop the corresponding conditional LP/dual with probability-weighted hard histories.
ideas.title: Conditional Suffix-Max LP
ideas.why_promising: It keeps the exact-comparator improvement from iteration 12 while moving back toward the original stochastic setting and naturally handles rare-history objections.

ideas.risks: May collapse into a restatement of the full LP. Stable comparators are sufficient but not necessary, and equal-revenue hard blocks are designed to defeat any small stable menu.
ideas.summary: Generalize the solver's stable-quote corollary. Study conditions under which one quote, a finite quote menu, or slowly varying near-optimal quotes b_T satisfy V_T^* - learner payoff = o(T) for all horizons. Use alternating paths, sparse spikes, and equal-revenue blocks as tests.
ideas.title: Argmax-Stability Conditions
ideas.why_promising: It explains why the alternating path is easy despite linear local suffix-menu cost and may yield readable sufficient conditions between the tautological LP and known loose bounds.

ideas.risks: The pseudo-regret comparator may exploit rare branches if their payoff is too large. Horizon accounting must ensure p_i N_i is negligible at all relevant horizons, not only block endpoints.
ideas.summary: Build a rare-event process where, conditional on a low-probability branch, a long equal-revenue block has kappa close to 1/e and long positive payoff delays, but the branch probability p_i makes its expected contribution p_i N_i=o(T_i). Compute beta, gamma, conditional kappa, Delta_T, and regret.
ideas.title: Rare Hard-Block Stress Test
ideas.why_promising: It would sharply demonstrate why essential-sup or unweighted local-hardness conditions are not necessary under expected pseudo-regret.

ideas.risks: Ordinary star discrepancy may not control monotone time-varying thresholds with weighted payoffs a_t 1{a_t<c_t}. A failed explicit construction would still leave only the nonconstructive theorem.
ideas.summary: Seek an explicit deterministic sequence replacing the probabilistic-method derandomization of the 1/e upper bound, for example a_t=exp(-u_t) with van der Corput, Kronecker, or other low-discrepancy u_t in [0,1]. Prove a uniform one-sided bound over nonincreasing threshold sequences.
ideas.title: Explicit Equal-Revenue Sequence
ideas.why_promising: It would make the deterministic 1/e known-path upper bound algorithmic and may improve the O(T^{2/3} sqrt log T) error term.

ideas.risks: This may be outside the intended exogenous model, and fully reactive adversaries can make the problem trivially impossible. The explorer should keep this as a boundary audit, not a replacement theorem.
ideas.summary: Probe the endogenous/reactive boundary. Construct examples where future prices depend on outstanding or realized quotes, so M_{t,T} is no longer independent of A_t and the suffix-max marginal formula fails. Identify which sufficiency and upper-bound claims survive only under exogeneity/counterfactual feedback.
ideas.title: Reactive-Price Boundary
ideas.why_promising: It clarifies whether the original delayed market-making model is purely exogenous; many accepted reductions rely on that assumption.

ideas.risks: The vector dimension grows with horizon, feedback is horizon-censored, and approachability may reproduce known delayed-learning bounds without a sharper characterization.
ideas.summary: Use the finite-prefix dual to define vector deficits indexed by horizons or comparator-threshold pairs, and ask whether Blackwell approachability or delayed approachability yields causal policies for unknown deterministic paths or stochastic kernels. Compare with Lagziel-Lehrer and calibration-decision-loss analogies.
ideas.title: Vector-Deficit Approachability
ideas.why_promising: It recasts one quote sequence serving many horizons as a standard simultaneous-objective problem and may produce algorithms or clean impossibility certificates.
